ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a cyclobutane four-membered carbon ring, and one carbon on the ring is connected to the right to a -CH2-, then connected to an amino nitrogen labeled NH2. On the right side is an independent nitrogen-oxygen-containing fragment, which can be read according to ordinary bond connectivity as O=N-O-N=O. There are also curved arrows in the figure indicating electron flow, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows; no ordinary covalent bond is drawn between the left amine and the right N-O fragment. Reasoning: The left component can be written as cyclobutane C1CCC1, with a -CH2NH2 substituent, and the equivalent SMILES is NCC1CCC1. The SMILES of the right component O=N-O-N=O is O=NON=O. The two components are not connected by ordinary bonds, so they are separated by a dot, giving NCC1CCC1.O=NON=O.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows? <image_1>

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and ignore all curved arrows/electron-flow annotations as instructed. Transcribe the left component: the cyclobutane ring is C1CCC1 and the explicit amine substituent is -CH2NH2 attached to a ring carbon, giving NCC1CCC1 in SMILES. Transcribe the right component as the linear heteroatom fragment O=N-O-N=O, giving O=NON=O. Since the two components are not connected by a drawn bond, join the two SMILES fragments with a dot to obtain NCC1CCC1.O=NON=O.
